source.title: Dream2Learn: Structured Generative Dreaming for Continual Learning

confidence_rationale: The architecture's own design choice -- generated ('dreamed') samples are never added to the replay buffer, only their prompts are retained -- is a real, independently-arrived-at instance of MECH-094's strict-gating principle (simulation content should not accumulate as committed experience). But the paper's larger purpose is to actively USE generated content as a productive self-training driver for representation reorganisation, a permissive stance MECH-094 does not itself endorse or address, and a measured 3.93% categorical-leakage rate shows the generated/real boundary is imperfect even under a design explicitly built to preserve it -- evidence that the separation MECH-094 requires is achievable but fragile in practice, not evidence that generated content should be granted experienced-event status.
failure_signatures: 3.93% of class replacements exhibited categorical leakage of future-class information from the frozen diffusion model's own prior knowledge -- the generated/novel boundary the method relies on is imperfect even when explicitly engineered.

Dreams are generated from a pre-trained diffusion model that may encode future concepts unknowingly, requiring a proposed mitigation of unlearning future-class concepts from the diffusion model via concept erasure -- an acknowledged, only partially-solved contamination risk.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Dream2Learn (D2L) has a classifier generate structured synthetic 'dreamed' training samples from its own internal representations via a frozen diffusion model conditioned through soft prompt optimization, producing novel, semantically distinct classes that do not correspond to previously observed data. The generated data are explicitly not used to replace memory: dreamed samples are never added to the replay buffer, only their prompts are retained as a persistent dream inventory. Instead, the dreamed classes expand and reorganize the representation space, supporting forward transfer to future tasks. Across Mini-ImageNet, FG-ImageNet, and ImageNet-R, D2L outperforms rehearsal-based baselines with positive forward transfer, though 3.93% of class replacements showed categorical leakage of future-class information from the diffusion model's own prior knowledge.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-094 asserts the system must maintain a functional distinction between simulation-mode content and real-experience content, such that simulation content does not accumulate in the viability map as committed experience -- failures of this distinction produce confabulation. Dream2Learn's explicit architectural choice to keep generated samples out of the persistent buffer (retaining only prompts, not the samples themselves, as committed content) is a clean, independently-motivated instance of exactly this principle in a different domain: a system that generates useful synthetic experience for representation reorganisation while deliberately refusing to let that content masquerade as accumulated real data. At the same time, the paper's larger project -- using generated self-training as a proactive, ongoing learning driver, not merely a passive buffer to be strictly gated -- is a stance MECH-094 neither requires nor forecloses, since REE's own sanctioned exception (MECH-322) already permits a narrow, conditional simulation-derived write path under specific value-tag and corroboration gating. The measured leakage rate is the most REE-relevant finding: even a system explicitly engineered to keep the simulation/real boundary clean leaks across it at a non-zero, measurable rate, which is a concrete illustration of exactly the failure mode MECH-094 exists to guard against.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a substantial domain gap: an image-classification continual-learning system with no analogue of REE's committed-experience/viability-map distinction, no clinical confabulation framing, and no default-mode/DMN write-profile machinery. The paper's positive framing (dreaming improves forward transfer) should not be read as evidence that generated content SHOULD be treated as equivalent to experienced events -- if anything, its explicit non-accumulation design and its leakage finding both cut toward caution, not permissiveness, about that equivalence. The mixed direction reflects this: the architecture's separation-by-design supports MECH-094's core principle, while the paper's underlying use case (actively mining generated content as a training driver) and its leakage result are each, in different ways, orthogonal-to-mildly-cautionary rather than straightforwardly confirming.
mapping.source_context: Image classification continual-learning benchmarks (Mini-ImageNet, FG-ImageNet, ImageNet-R); classifier paired with a frozen diffusion generative model conditioned via soft prompt optimization.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality is not preprint-capped: this is peer-reviewed IJCV (vol 134, issue 8, article 388), with solid multi-benchmark empirical validation. Mapping fidelity is capped low because the domain gap between ML continual-learning architecture design and REE's cognitive/clinical confabulation-failure framing is substantial -- the correspondence is at the level of a shared design principle, not a shared mechanism or failure mode. Transfer risk is high: image classification has no committed-experience/viability-map analogue, and the leakage finding, while informative, is specific to diffusion-model priors rather than obviously general to REE's own simulation-mode machinery.
